message.content:
Lions (*Panthera leo*) belong to the family **Felidae** (order Carnivora), while zebras (*Equus quagga*) belong to the family **Equidae** (order Perissodactyla).  
Both orders are part of the larger group **Laurasiatheria**, which is itself a clade within the placental mammals (Eutheria).

Therefore, the most recent common ancestor of a lion and a zebra is the last common ancestor of the superorder **Laurasiatheria**—an early mammal that lived roughly 90–100 million years ago. This ancestor gave rise to the lineages that eventually led to the carnivores (including felids) and the odd-toed ungulates (including equids).

The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want a biological answer. We can provide an explanation: lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) share a common ancestor within the order Carnivora? Wait, lions are mammals, specifically within the family Felidae, suborder Feliformia. Zebras are mammals, family Equidae, suborder Perissodactyla. So their common ancestor would be at the level of the class Mammalia, but more precisely the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria). But maybe they want the most recent common ancestor of the two species: that would be the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes both Feliformia and Perissodactyla. That might be the last common ancestor of the superorders Laurasiatheria? Actually, Felidae is part of the order Carnivora, which is part of the superorder Laurasiatheria. Equidae is part of the order Perissodactyla, also part of Laurasiatheria. So the last common ancestor of lions and zebras would be the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria. That ancestor lived around 90 million years ago. Alternatively, we could say the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which is older (~100-150 million years). But the question likely expects something like "the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae" or "the last common ancestor of the superorders Carnivora and Perissodactyla."
